verses.text: One shoot go come out of di stump of Jesse, and one branch from im roots go bear fruit.
Di Spirit of di Lord go rest on am: di spirit of wisdom and understanding, di spirit of counsel and might, di spirit of knowledge and of di fear of di Lord.
Im delight go be for di fear of di Lord. E no go judge by di sight of im eyes, neither decide by di hearing of im ears;
but with righteousness e go judge di poor, and decide with equity for di humble of di earth. E go strike di earth with di rod of im mouth, and with di breath of im lips e go kill di wicked.
Righteousness go be di belt of im waist, and faithfulness di belt of im loins.
Di wolf go live with di lamb, and di leopard go lie down with di young goat. Di calf, di young lion and di fattened calf go dey together, and small pikin go lead dem.
Di cow and di bear go feed. Dem young ones go lie down together. Di lion go eat straw like di ox.
Di nursing child go play by di hole of di cobra, and di weaned child go put im hand on di viper den.
Dem no go hurt or destroy for all my holy mountain, because di earth go full of di knowledge of di Lord, as di waters cover di sea.
For dat day, di root of Jesse, wey dey stand as banner for di peoples, na am di nations go seek, and im resting place go be glorious.

For dat day, di Lord go set im hand again di second time to recover di remnant of im people wey remain, from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath and from di islands of di sea.
E go set up banner for di nations, and go gather di outcasts of Israel, and gather together di dispersed of Judah from di four corners of di earth.
Di envy of Ephraim go depart, and dem wey dey trouble Judah go dey cut off. Ephraim no go envy Judah, and Judah no go trouble Ephraim.
Dem go fly down on di shoulder of di Philistines for di west. Together dem go plunder di people of di east. Dem go put dem hand on Edom and Moab, and di people of Ammon go obey dem.
Di Lord go utterly destroy di tongue of di Egyptian sea. With im mighty wind e go wave im hand over di River, and strike am into seven streams, and make men cross over dry-shod.
Dere go dey highway for di remnant of im people, wey go remain from Assyria, like e dey for Israel for di day wey e come up out of di land of Egypt.
For dat day you go talk say, “I go give thanks to you, Lord, because though you dey angry with me, your anger don turn away, and you comfort me.
See, God na my salvation. I go trust, and I no go dey afraid; because di Lord, di Lord, na my strength and my song; and e don become my salvation.”
So with joy una go draw water out of di wells of salvation.
For dat day una go talk say, “Give thanks to di Lord! Call on im name! Make im doings known among di peoples! Declare say im name dey exalted!
Sing to di Lord, because e don do excellent things. Make dis dey known for all di earth.
Cry aloud and shout, you inhabitant of Zion, because great na di Holy One of Israel for your middle.”
Di burden of Babylon, wey Isaiah, Amoz pikin, see.
Lift up banner upon di bare mountain. Raise di voice to dem. Wave di hand, make dem enter di gates of di nobles.
I don command my consecrated ones. Yes, I don call my mighty men for my anger, dem wey dey rejoice for my majesty.
Di noise of multitude for di mountains, like dat of great people! Di noise of di tumult of di kingdoms of di nations gathered together! Di Lord of Armies dey muster di army for battle.
Dem dey come from far country, from di uttermost part of heaven, even di Lord and di weapons of im indignation, to destroy di whole land.
Howl, because di day of di Lord dey at hand. E go come as destruction from di Almighty.
Therefore all hands go go limp, and every man heart go melt.
Dem go dey dismayed. Pangs and sorrows go seize dem. Dem go dey in pain as woman wey dey labour. Dem go look at one another in amazement. Dem faces go be faces of flame.
See, di day of di Lord dey come, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger, to make di land desolate, and to destroy di sinners out of am.
Because di stars of heaven and dem constellations no go give dem light. Di sun go dey darkened for im rising, and di moon no go cause im light to shine.
I go punish di world for im evil, and di wicked for dem iniquity. I go cause di arrogance of di proud to cease, and I go humble di haughtiness of di terrible.
I go make man more rare pass fine gold, even man pass di gold of Ophir.
Therefore I go shake di heavens, and di earth go move out of im place, for di wrath of di Lord of Armies, and for di day of im fierce anger.
Like gazelle wey dem dey chase, and like sheep wey nobody gather, dem go every man turn to im own people, and every man flee to im own land.
Everyone wey dem find go dey thrust through. Everyone wey dem catch go fall by di sword.
Dem infants go dey dashed in pieces before dem eyes. Dem houses go dey plundered, and dem wives ravished.
See, I go stir up di Medes against dem, wey no dey regard silver, and as for gold, dem no delight for am.
Dem bows go dash di young men in pieces. Dem no go have pity on di fruit of di womb. Dem eyes no go spare children.
Babylon, di glory of kingdoms, di beauty of di pride of di Chaldeans, go be like when God overthrow Sodom and Gomorrah.
E no go ever dey inhabited, neither e go dey dwelt in from generation to generation. Di Arabian no go pitch tent dere, neither shepherds go make dem flocks lie down dere.
But wild animals of di desert go lie dere, and dem houses go full of howling creatures. Ostriches go dwell dere, and wild goats go dance dere.
Hyenas go cry for dem fortresses, and jackals for dem pleasant palaces. Her time dey near to come, and her days no go dey prolonged.
Because di Lord go have compassion on Jacob, and go still choose Israel, and set dem for dem own land. Di foreigners go join dem, and dem go join di house of Jacob.

Di peoples go take dem and bring dem to dem place, and di house of Israel go possess dem for di land of di Lord as male servants and female servants. Dem go take captive dem wey take dem captive, and rule over dem oppressors.
For di day wey di Lord give you rest from your sorrow, from your trouble, and from di hard service wey dem make you serve,
you go take up dis proverb against di king of Babylon, and talk say, “How di oppressor don cease! How di golden city don cease!
Di Lord don break di staff of di wicked, di sceptre of di rulers,
wey strike di peoples for wrath with continual blows, wey rule di nations for anger, with persecution wey no restrain.
All di earth dey at rest, and dey quiet. Dem burst out into singing.
Yes, di cypress trees rejoice over you, and di cedars of Lebanon, dey talk say, ‘Since you don dey laid low, no woodcutter don come up against us.’
Sheol from beneath dey stirred up to meet you when you come. E stir up di spirits of di dead for you, even all di chief ones of di earth. E don raise up from dem thrones all di kings of di nations.
Dem all go answer and talk to you, ‘Una don become weak like us! Una don become like us!’
Your pomp don dey brought down to Sheol, with di sound of your harps. Maggots dey spread under you, and worms cover you.
How you don fall from heaven, morning star, son of di dawn! How you don dey cut down to di ground, you wey weaken di nations!
You talk for your heart, ‘I go ascend into heaven. I go exalt my throne above di stars of God. I go sit on di mount of assembly, for di far north.
I go ascend above di heights of di clouds. I go make myself like di Most High.’
Yet you go dey brought down to Sheol, to di depths of di pit.
Dem wey see you go stare at you, and consider you, say, ‘Na dis be di man wey make di earth tremble, wey shake kingdoms,
wey make di world like wilderness, and overthrow im cities, wey no release im prisoners go home?’
All di kings of di nations, all of dem, sleep for glory, everyone for im own tomb.

But you dey cast out of your tomb like abominable branch, like clothing of those wey dem kill, wey dem thrust through with sword, wey go down to di stones of di pit, like carcass wey dem trample underfoot.
You no go dey joined with dem for burial, because you don destroy your land. You don kill your people. Di offspring of evildoers no go dey named forever.
Prepare slaughter for im children because of di iniquity of dem fathers, so that dem no go rise up and possess di earth, and fill di surface of di world with cities.”
“I go rise up against dem,” talk di Lord of Armies, “and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, and son and son son,” talk di Lord.
“I go also make am possession for di porcupine, and pools of water. I go sweep am with di broom of destruction,” talk di Lord of Armies.
Di Lord of Armies don swear, say, “Surely as I don plan am, so e go be; and as I don purpose am, so e go stand,
say I go break di Assyrian for my land, and upon my mountains tread am underfoot. Den im yoke go depart from dem, and im burden go depart from dem shoulder.”
Dis na di purpose wey dem purpose against di whole earth, and dis na di hand wey dey stretched out over all di nations.
Because di Lord of Armies don purpose, and who go annul am? Im hand dey stretched out, and who go turn am back?
For di year wey King Ahaz die, dis burden come:
No rejoice, all Philistia, because di rod wey strike you don break, because from di serpent root go come out viper, and im offspring go be fiery flying serpent.
Di firstborn of di poor go feed, and di needy go lie down for safety. I go kill your root with famine, and im remnant go dey killed.
Howl, gate! Cry, city! Melt away, all Philistia! Because smoke dey come out of di north, and no straggler dey for im ranks.
Wetin dem go answer di messengers of di nation? Say di Lord don found Zion, and di afflicted of im people go take refuge inside am.
Di burden of Moab. Surely for di night Ar of Moab dey laid waste and brought to silence. Surely for di night Kir of Moab dey laid waste and brought to silence.
Dem don go up to Bayith and to Dibon, to di high places to weep. Moab dey wail over Nebo and over Medeba. Every head dey bald, and every beard cut off.
For dem streets dem don gird demselves with sackcloth. For dem housetops and for dem squares, everyone dey wail, dey weep abundantly.
Heshbon cry out, and Elealeh. Dem voice dey hear even to Jahaz. Therefore di armed men of Moab cry out. Im soul tremble inside am.
My heart cry out for Moab. Im fugitives flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah. Because by di ascent of Luhith dem go up with weeping. Because for di way of Horonaim dem raise cry of destruction.
Because di waters of Nimrim go dey desolate. Because di grass don wither, di new growth don fail. No green thing dey.
Therefore di abundance wey dem don get, and wetin dem don lay up, dem go carry go di brook of di willows.
Because di cry don go round di border of Moab. Im wailing reach Eglaim, and im wailing reach Beer Elim.
Because di waters of Dimon full of blood, yet I go bring more upon Dimon: lion upon dem wey escape of Moab, and upon di remnant of di land.
Send una di lambs to di ruler of di land, from Sela through di wilderness, to di mountain of di daughter of Zion.
Like wandering birds, like scattered nest, so di daughters of Moab go dey for di fords of di Arnon.
“Give counsel. Execute justice. Make your shade like night for di middle of noon. Hide di outcasts. No betray di fugitive.
Make my outcasts dwell with you. Moab, be shelter to dem from di face of di destroyer. For di extortioner don come to end, destruction don cease, di oppressors don consume out of di land.
Throne go dey established in mercy, and one go sit on am in truth, for di tent of David, judging, seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.”
We don hear of di pride of Moab: say e dey very proud; even of im arrogance, im pride and im wrath. Im boastings dey false.
Therefore make Moab wail for Moab. Everyone go wail. Una go mourn for di raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, as people wey dem don strike totally.

Because di fields of Heshbon don languish, and di vine of Sibmah. Di lords of di nations don break down im choice branches, wey reach even to Jazer, and wander through di wilderness. Im shoots stretch abroad and pass over di sea.
Therefore I go weep with di weeping of Jazer for di vine of Sibmah. I go water you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, because di shout over your summer fruits and over your harvest don fall.
Gladness dey taken away, and joy out of di fruitful field. For di vineyards no singing go dey, neither shouting. No treader go tread out wine for di presses. I don make di vintage shout cease.
Therefore my heart sound like harp for Moab, and my inward parts for Kir Heres.
E go happen say when Moab appear, when e weary imself for di high place, and come to im sanctuary to pray, e no go prevail.
Dis na di word wey di Lord don speak concerning Moab since dat time.

But now di Lord don speak, say, “Within three years, as di years of hired worker, di glory of Moab go dey brought into contempt, with all im great multitude, and di remnant go be very small and feeble.”
Di burden of Damascus. See, Damascus don cease to be city, and e go be ruinous heap.
Di cities of Aroer dey forsaken. Dem go be for flocks, wey go lie down, and nobody go make dem afraid.
Di fortress go cease from Ephraim, and di kingdom from Damascus, and di remnant of Syria. Dem go be like di glory of di children of Israel, talk di Lord of Armies.
For dat day di glory of Jacob go dey made thin, and di fatness of im flesh go grow lean.
E go be like when di reaper gather di standing grain, and im arm reap di ears. Yes, e go be like when one gather ears of grain for di valley of Rephaim.
Yet gleanings go remain inside am, like di shaking of di olive tree, two or three berries for di top of di uppermost bough, four or five for im most fruitful branches, talk di Lord, di God of Israel.
For dat day man go look to im Maker, and im eyes go have respect to di Holy One of Israel.
E no go look to di altars, di work of im hands, neither e go respect wetin im fingers don make, di Asherah poles and di incense altars.
For dat day im strong cities go be like di forsaken places of di woods and di mountain top, wey dem forsake because of di children of Israel, and e go be desolation.
Because you don forget di God of your salvation, and no remember di rock of your strength. Therefore you plant pleasant plants, and set am with foreign vine cuttings.
For di day wey you plant am, you make am grow, and for di morning you make your seed blossom; but di harvest go dey heaped up for di day of grief and desperate sorrow.
Woe to di multitude of many peoples, wey roar like di roaring of di seas! And di rushing of nations, wey rush like di rushing of mighty waters!

Di nations go rush like di rushing of many waters, but e go rebuke dem, and dem go flee far away, and go dey chased like di chaff of di mountains before di wind, and like whirling dust before di storm.
For evening time, see, terror! Before morning, dem no dey again. Dis na di portion of dem wey plunder us, and di lot of dem wey rob us.
Woe to di land of whirring wings, wey dey beyond di rivers of Cush;

wey send ambassadors by di sea, even in vessels of papyrus on di waters, say, “Go, una swift messengers, to nation wey tall and smooth, to people wey dey awesome from dem beginning onward, nation wey measure out and tread down, wey im land di rivers divide!”
All una inhabitants of di world, and una wey dwell for di earth, see as banner dey lifted up on di mountains, and hear as trumpet dey blow.
Because di Lord talk to me like dis: “I go dey quiet, and I go look from my dwelling place, like clear heat for sunshine, like cloud of dew for di heat of harvest.”
Because before harvest, when di blossom don finish, and di flower don become ripening grape, e go cut off di sprigs with pruning knives, and di spreading branches e go take away and cut down.
Dem go dey left together to di ravenous birds of di mountains, and to di animals of di earth. Di ravenous birds go summer upon dem, and all di animals of di earth go winter upon dem.

For dat time gift go dey brought to di Lord of Armies from people wey tall and smooth, from people wey dey awesome from dem beginning onward, nation wey measure out and tread down, wey im land di rivers divide, to di place of di name of di Lord of Armies, Mount Zion.
Di burden of Egypt. See, di Lord dey ride on swift cloud, and dey come to Egypt. Di idols of Egypt go tremble at im presence, and di heart of Egypt go melt inside am.
I go stir up Egyptians against Egyptians. Dem go fight, everyone against im brother, and everyone against im neighbour, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
Di spirit of Egypt go fail inside am. I go destroy im counsel. Dem go seek di idols, di charmers, di mediums and di wizards.
I go give di Egyptians over into di hand of cruel lord. Fierce king go rule over dem, talk di Lord, di Lord of Armies.
Di waters go dry up from di sea, and di river go waste and dry up.
Di rivers go stink. Di streams of Egypt go dey diminished and dry up. Di reeds and di rushes go wither.
Di meadows by di Nile, by di mouth of di Nile, and every sown field of di Nile go wither, dey driven away, and be no more.
Di fishermen go mourn, and all dem wey cast hook into di Nile go lament, and dem wey spread nets on di waters go languish.
Moreover dem wey work with combed flax, and dem wey weave white cloth, go dey ashamed.
Im pillars go dey crushed. All dem wey work for hire go dey grieved for soul.
Di princes of Zoan na only fools. Di counsel of Pharaoh wise counselors don become senseless. How una go talk to Pharaoh say, “I be di son of di wise, di son of ancient kings”?
Where dem dey? Where your wise men dey? Make dem tell you now, and make dem know wetin di Lord of Armies don purpose against Egypt.
Di princes of Zoan don become fools. Di princes of Memphis don dey deceived. Dem wey be di cornerstone of im tribes don cause Egypt to go astray.
Di Lord don mingle spirit of perverseness inside am. Dem don cause Egypt to go astray for every work of am, as drunken man stagger for im vomit.
Neither go dey any work for Egypt wey head or tail, palm branch or reed, fit do.
For dat day Egypt go be like women. E go tremble and fear because of di shaking of di hand of di Lord of Armies, wey e shake over am.
Di land of Judah go become terror to Egypt. Everyone to whom dem mention am go dey afraid, because of di purpose of di Lord of Armies, wey e purpose against am.
For dat day five cities for di land of Egypt go speak di language of Canaan, and swear to di Lord of Armies. One go dey called City of Destruction.
For dat day altar to di Lord go dey for di middle of di land of Egypt, and pillar to di Lord for im border.
E go be for sign and for witness to di Lord of Armies for di land of Egypt, because dem go cry to di Lord because of di oppressors, and e go send dem saviour, and great one, and e go deliver dem.
Di Lord go dey known to Egypt, and di Egyptians go know di Lord for dat day. Yes, dem go worship with sacrifice and offering, and dem go make vow to di Lord, and perform am.
Di Lord go strike Egypt, striking and healing. Dem go return to di Lord, and e go dey entreated by dem, and heal dem.
For dat day highway go dey from Egypt to Assyria, and di Assyrian go come into Egypt, and di Egyptian into Assyria, and di Egyptians go worship with di Assyrians.
For dat day Israel go be di third with Egypt and with Assyria, blessing for di middle of di earth,
because di Lord of Armies don bless am, say, “Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria di work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance.”
For di year wey Tartan come to Ashdod, when Sargon di king of Assyria send am, and e fight against Ashdod and capture am,
for dat time di Lord speak by Isaiah, Amoz pikin, say, “Go, and loose di sackcloth from your waist, and take your sandals off your feet.” E do so, walking naked and barefoot.
Di Lord talk, “Just as my servant Isaiah don waka naked and barefoot three years as sign and wonder against Egypt and against Cush,
so di king of Assyria go lead away di captives of Egypt, and di exiles of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with buttocks uncovered, to di shame of Egypt.
Dem go dey dismayed and ashamed, because of Cush dem hope, and of Egypt dem glory.
Di inhabitant of dis coast go talk for dat day, ‘See, na so e be with our hope, wia we flee for help to dey delivered from di king of Assyria! How we go escape?’”
